raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life — about 10 mu contracted to me. Around here, everyone does wheat and maize. That's the rotation. I don't know anything different, and the grain station buys it reliably. Cotton prices have been bad for years so I'm not touching that again. I'll keep a small patch near the house for vegetables — garlic and maybe some beans — like always, mostly for ourselves.

For wheat, I'll plant in October like normal. I buy the improved seed from the town supply shop — "济麦22" or whatever they're selling this year. It yields better than the old seed. For fertilizer I'll put down diammonium phosphate and urea at planting, then topdress urea at jointing. That's what I've always done. My neighbor puts on a bit more than me but I think I do okay. Water is getting harder to pump — the well is deeper every year — but I still need to water at winter, jointing, and heading at least. Four times if it's a dry spring.

After wheat harvest in June I'll plant maize right away. Rotary till and get the seed in fast. Maize doesn't need as much water — I'll water once if the summer rains are weak. One or two pesticide sprays for the corn borer, same as last year.

I won't change what works. I'm 56. I know this land.
